title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction & spillover paging optimizations to reduce fragmentation and OOMs
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: production hosts are experiencing elevated KV cache fragmentation and occasional OOMs when workloads exhibit many short-lived prefixes. This PR introduces an adaptive eviction policy plus a lightweight spillover pager to reduce memory amplification from fragmentation and to avoid synchronous evictions under load.

Summary of changes: introduces an adaptive score-based evictor that accounts for fragment size, last-access distribution, and estimated compactability; adds a spillover pager that streams cold KV shards to a configurable page store (SSD-backed) and keeps hot working sets in GPU memory; implements an on-the-fly compaction trigger that runs incrementally to reduce fragmentation without blocking inference; exposes new observability metrics and tuning knobs.

Benchmarks: internal microbench shows 25-40% reduction in steady-state memory footprint for churn-heavy workloads and a 3-8% improvement in p99 latency under sustained small-request traffic due to fewer blocking evictions. End-to-end cluster soak: no OOMs observed on a 48h stress run that previously triggered OOMs.

Testing: unit tests for eviction heuristics, integration tests for spillover pager and compaction, and end-to-end soak in perf-canary infra. CI: all checks passed after two CI reruns (flaky kernel compile on first run).

Rollout plan: feature-gated behind 'kv_adaptive_eviction_v2' with telemetry enabled; staged rollout to Dedicated clusters for two weeks, then global release. Backport candidate for next release if no regressions.

release_notes:
- Adaptive KV eviction reduces fragmentation and memory amplification for churn-heavy workloads.
- Spillover pager streams cold KV shards to disk to avoid OOMs and reduce worst-case blocking evictions.
- New metrics: kv_cache.evictions.adaptive_score, kv_cache.spillover.bytes_written, kv_cache.compaction.cycles.
- Feature gated behind kv_adaptive_eviction_v2.
benchmark_summary: Microbench (churn-heavy synthetic workload): memory footprint -35% median, 25-40% across tenants; p99 latency improved 3-8% due to reduced blocking evictions; compaction IO adds <=5ms per compaction slice. 48h soak: 0 OOMs (baseline had OOMs at ~12h).
testing: Unit tests covering scoring heuristics and boundary conditions; integration tests for pager write/read correctness and crash recovery; perf-canary soak run validated stability. CI matrix covers linux-x86_64 with and without SSD page store enabled.
